caption: The image is a black-and-white photograph of a large ceramic pitcher. The pitcher is light in color, likely white or off-white, with dark printed illustrations and text on its surface. The most prominent decoration is on the front: a large American heraldic eagle with outspread wings, holding arrows and an olive branch. The eagle's chest is covered by a shield patterned with vertical stripes, and above the eagle is a row of stars with a banner reading "E Pluribus Unum." A semi-circular text surrounds the image, including the name "Jefferson" and the year "1802," along with an inscription mentioning "Peace, Commerce, and honest Friendship with all Nations." To the left side of the eagle is an oval medallion containing a skull and crossbones motif. On either side of the pitcher, near the base, are small landscape vignettes with animals, one of which appears to show a lamb lying down, and another shows a horse standing on grass. Near the top right, above a slender plant or branch design, is another animal illustration. The rim of the pitcher appears slightly chipped, and there is a thin, dark band encircling the rim and base for added decoration. The overall composition consists of fine, detailed linework and printed motifs applied to the curved surface of the ceramic piece.
title: Liverpool Jug
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
